## Data Driven Content / Nodes

The data-driven content feature was introduced to solve a specific structural problem. The Sites tree is very important as it reflects ZAP's understanding of the application structure. If it is not a good representation of the structure then ZAP will not be able to attack the application effectively. Some applications include data in URL paths — these URLs represent the same page but with different data, yet by default ZAP will represent them as separate nodes.

This is a problem because if you have hundreds or thousands of pages like this it will significantly increase the time it takes to scan the application. In ZAP terms these are 'data driven content' — URL parameters that contain data instead of representing part of the application structure.
